newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean think tank sees 6.5 pct GDP growth in '97.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean think tank sees 6.5 pct GDP growth in '97.

text.p: South Korea's gross domestic product (GDP) growth is expected to slow to around 6.5 percent in calendar 1997 from this year's estimated 6.8 percent rise, a state-run think tank said on Tuesday in a report.
The Korea Development Institute's report said the nation's economy was expected to see exports gradually recovering from the second half of 1997.
The government's latest projection for this year's economic growth was set at seven percent, following a nine percent growth in 1995 and an 8.6 percent rise in 1994.
The report predicted the nation's current account deficit to reach $18.8 billion for this year and $13.2 billion for next year, compared with an $8.8 billion shortfall in 1995.
It said annual inflation, measured by the consumer price index (CPI) growth, was estimated at 4.5 percent this year and 4.3 percent in 1997, compared with a 4.7 percent rise in 1995.
